Validation\n+\n+| Field  | Value                |\n+| ------ | -------------------- |\n+| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |\n+| Status | In Progress          |\n+\n+Every tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor. When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget.\n+\n+## Validation at execute time\n+\n+- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16)).\n+- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46)).\n+- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults.\n+- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake.\n+\n+## Schema compilation and caching\n+\n+- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94)).\n+- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema`.\n+- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules.\n+\n+## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery\n+\n+- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112)).\ndiff --git static create(max: number): StackLike {\\n    const HeapCls = getUintArray(max)\\n    if (!HeapCls) return []\\n    Stack.#constructing = true\\n    const s = new Stack(max, HeapCls)\\n * @module LRUCache\\n */\\n\\n// module-private names and types\\ntype Perf = { now: () => number }\\nconst perf: Perf =\\n  typeof performance === 'object' &&\\n  performance &&\\n  typeof performance.now === 'function'\\n    ? performance\\n    : Date\\n\\nconst warned = new Set<string>()\\n\\n// either a function or a class\\ntype ForC = ((...a: any[]) => any) | { new (...a: any[]): any }\\n\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst PROCESS = (\\n  typeof process === 'object' && !!process ? process : {}\\n) as { [k: string]: any }\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\n\\nconst emitWarning = (\\n  msg: string,\\n  type: string,\\n  code: string,\\n  fn: ForC\\n) => {\\n  typeof PROCESS.emitWarning === 'function'\\n    ? PROCESS.emitWarning(msg, type, code, fn)\\n    : console.error(`[${code}] ${type}: ${msg}`)\\n}\\n\\nlet AC = globalThis.AbortController\\nlet AS = globalThis.AbortSignal\\n\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nif (typeof AC === 'undefined') {\\n  //@ts-ignore\\n  AS = class AbortSignal {\\n    onabort?: (...a: any[]) => any\\n    _onabort: ((...a: any[]) => any)[] = []\\n    reason?: any\\n    aborted: boolean = false\\n    addEventListener(_: string, fn: (...a: any[]) => any) {\\n      this._onabort.push(fn)\\n    }\\n  }\\n  //@ts-ignore\\n  AC = class AbortController {\\n    constructor() {\\n      warnACPolyfill()\\n    }\\n    signal = new AS()\\n    abort(reason: any) {\\n      if (this.signal.aborted) return\\n      //@ts-ignore\\n      this.signal.reason = reason\\n      //@ts-ignore\\n      this.signal.aborted = true\\n      //@ts-ignore\\n      for (const fn of this.signal._onabort) {\\n        fn(reason)\\n      }\\n      this.signal.onabort?.(reason)\\n    }\\n  }\\n  let printACPolyfillWarning =\\n    PROCESS.env?.LRU_CACHE_IGNORE_AC_WARNING !== '1'\\n  const warnACPolyfill = () => {\\n    if (!printACPolyfillWarning) return\\n    printACPolyfillWarning = false\\n    emitWarning(\\n      'AbortController is not defined. If using lru-cache in ' +\\n        'node 14, load an AbortController polyfill from the ' +\\n        '`node-abort-controller` package. A minimal polyfill is ' +\\n        'provided for use by LRUCache.fetch(), but it should not be ' +\\n        'relied upon in other contexts (eg, passing it to other APIs that ' +\\n        'use AbortController/AbortSignal might have undesirable effects). * @module LRUCache\\n */\\n\\nimport { metrics, tracing } from './diagnostics-channel.js'\\nimport { defaultPerf } from './perf.js'\\nimport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\nexport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\n\\nconst hasSubscribers = () =>\\n  metrics.hasSubscribers || tracing.hasSubscribers\\n\\nconst warned = new Set<string>()\\n\\n// either a function or a class\\n// oxlint-disable-next-line no-explicit-any\\ntype ForC = ((...a: any[]) => any) | { new (...a: any[]): any }\\n\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst PROCESS = (\\n  typeof process === 'object' && !!process ?\\n    process\\n  : {}) as { [k: string]: unknown }\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nconst emitWarning = (\\n  msg: string,\\n  type: string,\\n  code: string,\\n  fn: ForC,\\n) => {\\n  if (typeof PROCESS.emitWarning === 'function') {\\n    PROCESS.emitWarning(msg, type, code, fn)\\n  } else {\\n    //oxlint-disable-next-line no-console\\n    console.error(`[${code}] ${type}: ${msg}`)\\n  }\\n}\\nconst shouldWarn = (code: string) => !warned.has(code)\\n\\nconst TYPE = Symbol('type')\\nexport type PosInt = number & { [TYPE]: 'Positive Integer' }\\nexport type Index = number & { [TYPE]: 'LRUCache Index' }\\n\\nconst isPosInt = (n: unknown): n is PosInt =>\\n  !!n && n === Math.floor(n as number) && n > 0 && isFinite(n)\\n\\nexport type UintArray = Uint8Array | Uint16Array | Uint32Array\\nexport type NumberArray = UintArray | number[]\\n\\n// This is a little bit ridiculous, tbh.\\n// The maximum array length is 2^32-1 or thereabouts on most JS impls.\\n// And well before that point, you're caching the entire world, I mean,\\n// that's ~32GB of just integers for the next/prev links, plus whatever\\n// else to hold that many keys and values.  Just filling the memory with\\n// zeroes at init time is brutal when you get that big.\\n// But why not be complete?\\n// Maybe in the future, these limits will have expanded.\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst getUintArray = (max: number) =>\\n  !isPosInt(max) ? null\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 8) ? Uint8Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 16) ? Uint16Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 32) ? Uint32Array\\n  : max <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER ? ZeroArray\\n  : null\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nclass ZeroArray extends Array<number> {\\n  constructor(size: number) {\\n    super(size)\\n    this.fill(0)\\n  }\\n}\\nexport type { ZeroArray }\\nexport type { Stack }\\n\\nexport type StackLike = Stack | Index[]\\nclass Stack {\\n  /* c8 ignore start - not sure why this is showing up uncovered?? */\\n  heap: NumberArray\\n  /* c8 ignore stop */\\n  length: number\\n  // private constructor\\n  static #constructing: boolean = false\\n  static create(max: number): StackLike {\\n    const HeapCls = getUintArray(max)\\n    if (!HeapCls) return []\\n    Stack.#constructing = true\\n    const s = new Stack(max, HeapCls)\\n    Stack.#constructing = false\\n    return s\\n  }\\n  constructor(max: number, HeapCls: { new (n: number): NumberArray }) {\\n    /* c8 ignore start */\\n    if (!Stack.#constructing) {\\n      throw new TypeError('instantiate Stack using Stack.create(n)')\\n    }\\n    /* c8 ignore stop */\\n    this.heap = new HeapCls(max)\\n    this.length = 0\\n  }\\n  push(n: Index) {\\n    this.heap[this.length++] = n\\n  }\\n  pop(): Index {\\n    return this.heap[--this.length] as Index\\n  }\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * Promise representing an in-progress {@link LRUCache#fetch} call\\n */\\nexport type BackgroundFetch<V> = Promise<V | undefined> & {\\n  __returned: BackgroundFetch<V> | undefined\\n  __abortController: AbortController\\n  __staleWhileFetching: V | undefined\\n}\\n\\nexport type DisposeTask<K, V> = [\\n  value: V,\\n  key: K,\\n  reason: LRUCache.DisposeReason,\\n]\\n\\nexport namespace LRUCache {\\n  /**\\n   * An integer greater than 0, reflecting the calculated size of items\\n   */\\n  export type Size = number\\n\\n  /**\\n   * Integer greater than 0, representing some number of milliseconds, or the\\n   * time at which a TTL started counting from.\\n   */\\n  export type Milliseconds = number\\n\\n  /**\\n   * An integer greater than 0, reflecting a number of items\\n   */\\n  export type Count = number\\n\\n  /**\\n   * The reason why an item was removed from the cache, passed\\n   * to the {@link Disposer} methods.\\n   *\\n   * - `evict`: The item was evicted because it is the least recently used,\\n   *   and the cache is full.\\n   * - `set`: A new value was set, overwriting the old value being disposed.\\n   * - `delete`: The item was explicitly deleted, either by calling\\n   *   {@link LRUCache#delete}, {@link LRUCache#clear}, or\\n   *   {@link LRUCache#set} with an undefined value.\\n   * - `expire`: The item was removed due to exceeding its TTL.\\n   * - `fetch`: A {@link OptionsBase#fetchMethod} operation returned\\n   *   `undefined` or was aborted, causing the item to be deleted.\\n   */\\n  export type DisposeReason =\\n    | 'evict'\\n    | 'set'\\n    | 'delete'\\n    | 'expire'\\n    | 'fetch'\\n  /**\\n   * A method called upon item removal, passed as the\\n   * {@link OptionsBase.dispose} and/or\\n   * {@link OptionsBase.disposeAfter} options.\\n   */\\n  export type Disposer<K, V> = (\\n    value: V,\\n    key: K,\\n    reason: DisposeReason,\\n  ) => void\\n\\n  /**\\n   * The reason why an item was added to the cache, passed\\n   * to the {@link Inserter} methods.\\n   *\\n   * - `add`: the item was not found in the cache, and was added\\n   * - `update`: the item was in the cache, with the same value provided\\n   * - `replace`: the item was in the cache, and replaced\\n   */\\n  export type InsertReason = 'add' | 'update' | 'replace'\\n\\n  /**\\n   * A method called upon item insertion, passed as the\\n   * {@link OptionsBase.insert}\\n   */\\n  export type Inserter<K, V> = (\\n    value: V,\\n    key: K,\\n    reason: InsertReason,\\n  ) => void\\n\\n  /**\\n   * A function that returns the effective calculated size\\n   * of an entry in the cache.\\n   */\\n  export type SizeCalculator<K, V> = (value: V, key: K) => Size\\n\\n  /**\\n   * Options provided to the\\n   * {@link OptionsBase.fetchMethod} function.\\n   */\\n  export interface FetcherOptions<K, V, FC = unknown> {\\n    signal: AbortSignal\\n    options: FetcherFetchOptions<K, V, FC>\\n    /**\\n     * Object provided in the {@link FetchOptions.context} option to\\n     * {@link LRUCache#fetch}\\n     */\\n    context: FC\\n  }\\n\\n  /**\\n   * Occasionally, it may be useful to track the internal behavior of the\\n   * cache, particularly for logging, debugging, or for behavior within the\\n   * `fetchMethod`. To do this, you can pass a `status` object to the\\n   * {@link LRUCache#fetch}, {@link LRUCache#get}, {@link LRUCache#set},\\n   * {@link LRUCache#memo}, and {@link LRUCache#has} methods.\\n   *\\n   * The `status` option should be a plain JavaScript object. The following\\n   * fields will be set on it appropriately, depending on the situation.\\n   *\\n   * These objects are also the context objects passed to listeners on the\\n   * `lru-cache:metrics` diagnostic channel, and the `lru-cache` tracing\\n   * channels, in platforms that support them.\\n   */\\n  export interface Status<K, V, FC = unknown> {\\n    /**\\n     * The operation being performed\\n     */\\n    op?: 'get' | 'set' | 'memo' | 'fetch' | 'delete' | 'has' | 'peek'\\n    /**\\n     * The status of a set() operation.\\n     *\\n     * - add: the item was not found in the cache, and was added\\n     * - update: the item was in the cache, with the same value provided\\n     * - replace: the item was in the cache, and replaced\\n     * - * @module LRUCache\\n */\\n\\nimport { metrics, tracing } from './diagnostics-channel.js'\\nimport { defaultPerf } from './perf.js'\\nimport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\nexport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\n\\nconst hasSubscribers = () =>\\n  metrics.hasSubscribers || tracing.hasSubscribers\\n\\nconst warned = new Set<string>()\\n\\n// either a function or a class\\n// oxlint-disable-next-line no-explicit-any\\ntype ForC = ((...a: any[]) => any) | { new (...a: any[]): any }\\n\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst PROCESS = (\\n  typeof process === 'object' && !!process ?\\n    process\\n  : {}) as { [k: string]: unknown }\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nconst emitWarning = (\\n  msg: string,\\n  type: string,\\n  code: string,\\n  fn: ForC,\\n) => {\\n  if (typeof PROCESS.emitWarning === 'function') {\\n    PROCESS.emitWarning(msg, type, code, fn)\\n  } else {\\n    //oxlint-disable-next-line no-console\\n    console.error(`[${code}] ${type}: ${msg}`)\\n  }\\n}\\nconst shouldWarn = (code: string) => !warned.has(code)\\n\\nconst TYPE = Symbol('type')\\nexport type PosInt = number & { [TYPE]: 'Positive Integer' }\\nexport type Index = number & { [TYPE]: 'LRUCache Index' }\\n\\nconst isPosInt = (n: unknown): n is PosInt =>\\n  !!n && n === Math.floor(n as number) && n > 0 && isFinite(n)\\n\\nexport type UintArray = Uint8Array | Uint16Array | Uint32Array\\nexport type NumberArray = UintArray | number[]\\n\\n// This is a little bit ridiculous, tbh.\\n// The maximum array length is 2^32-1 or thereabouts on most JS impls.\\n// And well before that point, you're caching the entire world, I mean,\\n// that's ~32GB of just integers for the next/prev links, plus whatever\\n// else to hold that many keys and values.  Just filling the memory with\\n// zeroes at init time is brutal when you get that big.\\n// But why not be complete?\\n// Maybe in the future, these limits will have expanded.\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst getUintArray = (max: number) =>\\n  !isPosInt(max) ? null\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 8) ? Uint8Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 16) ? Uint16Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 32) ? Uint32Array\\n  : max <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER ? ZeroArray\\n  : null\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nclass ZeroArray extends Array<number> {\\n  constructor(size: number) {\\n    super(size)\\n    this.fill(0)\\n  }\\n}\\nexport type { ZeroArray }\\nexport type { Stack }\\n\\nexport type StackLike = Stack | Index[]\\nclass Stack {\\n  /* c8 ignore start - * @module LRUCache\\n */\\n\\nimport { metrics, tracing } from './diagnostics-channel.js'\\nimport { defaultPerf } from './perf.js'\\nimport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\nexport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\n\\nconst hasSubscribers = () =>\\n  metrics.hasSubscribers || tracing.hasSubscribers\\n\\nconst warned = new Set<string>()\\n\\n// either a function or a class\\n// oxlint-disable-next-line no-explicit-any\\ntype ForC = ((...a: any[]) => any) | { new (...a: any[]): any }\\n\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst PROCESS = (\\n  typeof process === 'object' && !!process ?\\n    process\\n  : {}) as { [k: string]: unknown }\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nconst emitWarning = (\\n  msg: string,\\n  type: string,\\n  code: string,\\n  fn: ForC,\\n) => {\\n  if (typeof PROCESS.emitWarning === 'function') {\\n    PROCESS.emitWarning(msg, type, code, fn)\\n  } else {\\n    //oxlint-disable-next-line no-console\\n    console.error(`[${code}] ${type}: ${msg}`)\\n  }\\n}\\nconst shouldWarn = (code: string) => !warned.has(code)\\n\\nconst TYPE = Symbol('type')\\nexport type PosInt = number & { [TYPE]: 'Positive Integer' }\\nexport type Index = number & { [TYPE]: 'LRUCache Index' }\\n\\nconst isPosInt = (n: unknown): n is PosInt =>\\n  !!n && n === Math.floor(n as number) && n > 0 && isFinite(n)\\n\\nexport type UintArray = Uint8Array | Uint16Array | Uint32Array\\nexport type NumberArray = UintArray | number[]\\n\\n// This is a little bit ridiculous, tbh.\\n// The maximum array length is 2^32-1 or thereabouts on most JS impls.\\n// And well before that point, you're caching the entire world, I mean,\\n// that's ~32GB of just integers for the next/prev links, plus whatever\\n// else to hold that many keys and values.  Just filling the memory with\\n// zeroes at init time is brutal when you get that big.\\n// But why not be complete?\\n// Maybe in the future, these limits will have expanded.\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst getUintArray = (max: number) =>\\n  !isPosInt(max) ? null\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 8) ? Uint8Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 16) ? Uint16Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 32) ? Uint32Array\\n  : max <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER ? ZeroArray\\n  : null\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nclass ZeroArray extends Array<number> {\\n  constructor(size: number) {\\n    super(size)\\n    this.fill(0)\\n  }\\n}\\nexport type { ZeroArray }\\nexport type { Stack }\\n\\nexport type StackLike = Stack | Index[]\\nclass Stack {\\n  /* c8 ignore start - * @module LRUCache\\n */\\n\\nimport { metrics, tracing } from './diagnostics-channel.js'\\nimport { defaultPerf } from './perf.js'\\nimport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\nexport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\n\\nconst hasSubscribers = () =>\\n  metrics.hasSubscribers || tracing.hasSubscribers\\n\\nconst warned = new Set<string>()\\n\\n// either a function or a class\\n// oxlint-disable-next-line no-explicit-any\\ntype ForC = ((...a: any[]) => any) | { new (...a: any[]): any }\\n\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst PROCESS = (\\n  typeof process === 'object' && !!process ?\\n    process\\n  : {}) as { [k: string]: unknown }\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nconst emitWarning = (\\n  msg: string,\\n  type: string,\\n  code: string,\\n  fn: ForC,\\n) => {\\n  if (typeof PROCESS.emitWarning === 'function') {\\n    PROCESS.emitWarning(msg, type, code, fn)\\n  } else {\\n    //oxlint-disable-next-line no-console\\n    console.error(`[${code}] ${type}: ${msg}`)\\n  }\\n}\\nconst shouldWarn = (code: string) => !warned.has(code)\\n\\nconst TYPE = Symbol('type')\\nexport type PosInt = number & { [TYPE]: 'Positive Integer' }\\nexport type Index = number & { [TYPE]: 'LRUCache Index' }\\n\\nconst isPosInt = (n: unknown): n is PosInt =>\\n  !!n && n === Math.floor(n as number) && n > 0 && isFinite(n)\\n\\nexport type UintArray = Uint8Array | Uint16Array | Uint32Array\\nexport type NumberArray = UintArray | number[]\\n\\n// This is a little bit ridiculous, tbh.\\n// The maximum array length is 2^32-1 or thereabouts on most JS impls.\\n// And well before that point, you're caching the entire world, I mean,\\n// that's ~32GB of just integers for the next/prev links, plus whatever\\n// else to hold that many keys and values.  Just filling the memory with\\n// zeroes at init time is brutal when you get that big.\\n// But why not be complete?\\n// Maybe in the future, these limits will have expanded.\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst getUintArray = (max: number) =>\\n  !isPosInt(max) ? null\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 8) ? Uint8Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 16) ? Uint16Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 32) ? Uint32Array\\n  : max <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER ? ZeroArray\\n  : null\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nclass ZeroArray extends Array<number> {\\n  constructor(size: number) {\\n    super(size)\\n    this.fill(0)\\n  }\\n}\\nexport type { ZeroArray }\\nexport type { Stack }\\n\\nexport type StackLike = Stack | Index[]\\nclass Stack {\\n  /* c8 ignore start - * @module LRUCache\\n */\\n\\nimport { metrics, tracing } from './diagnostics-channel.js'\\nimport { defaultPerf } from './perf.js'\\nimport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\nexport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\n\\nconst hasSubscribers = () =>\\n  metrics.hasSubscribers || tracing.hasSubscribers\\n\\nconst warned = new Set<string>()\\n\\n// either a function or a class\\n// oxlint-disable-next-line no-explicit-any\\ntype ForC = ((...a: any[]) => any) | { new (...a: any[]): any }\\n\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst PROCESS = (\\n  typeof process === 'object' && !!process ?\\n    process\\n  : {}) as { [k: string]: unknown }\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nconst emitWarning = (\\n  msg: string,\\n  type: string,\\n  code: string,\\n  fn: ForC,\\n) => {\\n  if (typeof PROCESS.emitWarning === 'function') {\\n    PROCESS.emitWarning(msg, type, code, fn)\\n  } else {\\n    //oxlint-disable-next-line no-console\\n    console.error(`[${code}] ${type}: ${msg}`)\\n  }\\n}\\nconst shouldWarn = (code: string) => !warned.has(code)\\n\\nconst TYPE = Symbol('type')\\nexport type PosInt = number & { [TYPE]: 'Positive Integer' }\\nexport type Index = number & { [TYPE]: 'LRUCache Index' }\\n\\nconst isPosInt = (n: unknown): n is PosInt =>\\n  !!n && n === Math.floor(n as number) && n > 0 && isFinite(n)\\n\\nexport type UintArray = Uint8Array | Uint16Array | Uint32Array\\nexport type NumberArray = UintArray | number[]\\n\\n// This is a little bit ridiculous, tbh.\\n// The maximum array length is 2^32-1 or thereabouts on most JS impls.\\n// And well before that point, you're caching the entire world, I mean,\\n// that's ~32GB of just integers for the next/prev links, plus whatever\\n// else to hold that many keys and values.  Just filling the memory with\\n// zeroes at init time is brutal when you get that big.\\n// But why not be complete?\\n// Maybe in the future, these limits will have expanded.\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst getUintArray = (max: number) =>\\n  !isPosInt(max) ? null\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 8) ? Uint8Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 16) ? Uint16Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 32) ? Uint32Array\\n  : max <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER ? ZeroArray\\n  : null\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nclass ZeroArray extends Array<number> {\\n  constructor(size: number) {\\n    super(size)\\n    this.fill(0)\\n  }\\n}\\nexport type { ZeroArray }\\nexport type { Stack }\\n\\nexport type StackLike = Stack | Index[]\\nclass Stack {\\n  /* c8 ignore start - * @module LRUCache\\n */\\n\\nimport { metrics, tracing } from './diagnostics-channel.js'\\nimport { defaultPerf } from './perf.js'\\nimport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\nexport type { Perf } from './perf.js'\\n\\nconst hasSubscribers = () =>\\n  metrics.hasSubscribers || tracing.hasSubscribers\\n\\nconst warned = new Set<string>()\\n\\n// either a function or a class\\n// oxlint-disable-next-line no-explicit-any\\ntype ForC = ((...a: any[]) => any) | { new (...a: any[]): any }\\n\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst PROCESS = (\\n  typeof process === 'object' && !!process ?\\n    process\\n  : {}) as { [k: string]: unknown }\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nconst emitWarning = (\\n  msg: string,\\n  type: string,\\n  code: string,\\n  fn: ForC,\\n) => {\\n  if (typeof PROCESS.emitWarning === 'function') {\\n    PROCESS.emitWarning(msg, type, code, fn)\\n  } else {\\n    //oxlint-disable-next-line no-console\\n    console.error(`[${code}] ${type}: ${msg}`)\\n  }\\n}\\nconst shouldWarn = (code: string) => !warned.has(code)\\n\\nconst TYPE = Symbol('type')\\nexport type PosInt = number & { [TYPE]: 'Positive Integer' }\\nexport type Index = number & { [TYPE]: 'LRUCache Index' }\\n\\nconst isPosInt = (n: unknown): n is PosInt =>\\n  !!n && n === Math.floor(n as number) && n > 0 && isFinite(n)\\n\\nexport type UintArray = Uint8Array | Uint16Array | Uint32Array\\nexport type NumberArray = UintArray | number[]\\n\\n// This is a little bit ridiculous, tbh.\\n// The maximum array length is 2^32-1 or thereabouts on most JS impls.\\n// And well before that point, you're caching the entire world, I mean,\\n// that's ~32GB of just integers for the next/prev links, plus whatever\\n// else to hold that many keys and values.  Just filling the memory with\\n// zeroes at init time is brutal when you get that big.\\n// But why not be complete?\\n// Maybe in the future, these limits will have expanded.\\n/* c8 ignore start */\\nconst getUintArray = (max: number) =>\\n  !isPosInt(max) ? null\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 8) ? Uint8Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 16) ? Uint16Array\\n  : max <= Math.pow(2, 32) ? Uint32Array\\n  : max <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER ? ZeroArray\\n  : null\\n/* c8 ignore stop */\\n\\nclass ZeroArray extends Array<number> {\\n  constructor(size: number) {\\n    super(size)\\n    this.fill(0)\\n  }\\n}\\nexport type { ZeroArray }\\nexport type { Stack }\\n\\nexport type StackLike = Stack | Index[]\\nclass Stack {\\n  /* c8 ignore start - 'is invalid'}` : (err.message ?? 'invalid input');\n    });\n    return `Invalid input for tool \"${toolName}\": ${descriptions.join('; ')}`;\n  }","file_path":"target/src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts","new_string":"  private formatValidationErrors(toolName: string, errors?: readonly unknown[] | null): string {\n    if (!errors || errors.length === 0) {\n      return `Invalid input for tool \"${toolName}\"`;\n    }\n    const descriptions: string[] = [];\n    for (const err of errors) {\n      if (!isRecord(err)) {\n        continue;\n      }\n      const rawPath =\n        typeof err.instancePath === 'string'\n          ? err.instancePath\n          : typeof err.dataPath === 'string'\n            ? err.dataPath\n            : '';\n      const params = isRecord(err.params) ? err.params : undefined;\n      const missingProp = typeof params?.missingProperty === 'string' ? params.missingProperty : '';\n      const fieldPath = rawPath ? cleanInstancePath(rawPath) : missingProp;\n\n      if (err.keyword === 'required' && missingProp) {\n        descriptions.push(`missing required property \"${missingProp}\"`);\n      } else if (err.keyword === 'type' && typeof params?.type === 'string') {\n        descriptions.push(`property \"${fieldPath}\" must be of type ${params.type}`);\n      } else if (err.keyword === 'enum' && Array.isArray(params?.allowedValues)) {\n        descriptions.push(`property \"${fieldPath}\" must be one of allowed values`);\n      } else {\n        const msg = typeof err.message === 'string' ? err.message : 'is invalid';\n        descriptions.push(fieldPath ? `property \"${fieldPath}\" ${msg}` : msg);\n      }\n    }\n    if (descriptions.length === 0) {\n      return `Invalid input for tool \"${toolName}\"`;\n    }\n    return `Invalid input for tool \"${toolName}\": ${descriptions.join('; ')}`;\n  }"}}
